candidates.exact_span: For the analysis, EPA used the San Juan River geometric mean hardness of 132 mg/l (expressed as CaCO3) provided by NMED.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the hardness value used in limit derivation is interpreted differently (source, expression as CaCO3, or applicability to this discharge), the derived numeric cyanide limits or their basis could change, altering which enforceable limit applies for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The results of Navajo Nation RP screening (see Appendix 3) show Cyanide pollutant demonstrates RP to exceed the Navajo Nation water quality standards consistent with the designated uses for the receiving water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cyanide is treated as having reasonable potential and subject to water-quality-based numeric limits depends on interpreting this RP finding and its tie to designated uses; a different reading could change whether numeric limits are applicable at all.

candidates.exact_span: As indicated, the draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L, respectively, for Cyanide.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated daily maximum and monthly average values are the operative numeric limits for exceedance analysis; interpreting which limit type applies to a given monitoring period or measurement type would change compliance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall have a 1-year compliance schedule to achieve final limitations for Cyanide pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A compliance schedule implies final cyanide limits may not be immediately enforceable; interpreting when the schedule starts and whether interim versus final limits govern FY2025 measurements would change applicable-limit analysis (A) and whether missing or interim-period results reflect required monitoring or unresolved compliance states (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permit will require compliance schedule reports.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpreting compliance schedule reporting as a distinct monitoring obligation affects which requirements were applicable during FY2025 (B) and how periods without ordinary numeric results should be classified when only schedule-report evidence exists (C).

candidates.exact_span: Technology based pollutants; BOD5 and TSS, are proposed to be monitored five times per week, with sampling on at least five different days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The five-times-per-week frequency and five-different-days constraint define how many BOD5 and TSS monitoring events were required in FY2025; a different reading of frequency or day-distribution rules would change obligation counts and adequacy assessments.

candidates.exact_span: Flow is proposed to be monitored continuously using a totalizing meter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Continuous totalizing-meter flow monitoring sets a different obligation standard than periodic sampling; interpreting 'continuous' and the meter requirement affects whether flow monitoring was required for each period in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Sample type for BOD5 and TSS is 12-Hr composite.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Composite sample type governs how BOD5/TSS measurements must be collected and whether reported values are comparable to permit limits (A) and whether absent or non-conforming samples reflect unfulfilled monitoring obligations (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: The monitoring frequencies of daily for TRC and five times per week for E. coli, pH and flow are consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Daily versus five-times-per-week frequencies for TRC, E. coli, pH, and flow directly determine expected monitoring counts in FY2025; interpreting which parameters carry which frequency changes obligation applicability.

candidates.exact_span: Report requirements of once per week for TDS is also consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A weekly TDS report requirement may be report-only rather than a numeric compliance limit; interpreting it as monitoring versus reporting affects obligation tracking (B) and whether missing TDS data implies a compliance gap or a different no-data category (C).

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will not propose any WET limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Absence of proposed WET numeric limits means no ordinary numeric exceedance comparison applies to WET results; interpreting whether any WET-derived limit nonetheless applies would change limit-applicability rows.

candidates.exact_span: However, continuation of WET monitoring is proposed in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Continued WET monitoring despite no numeric limits establishes an ongoing monitoring obligation whose applicability in FY2025 must be resolved separately from limit analysis.

candidates.exact_span: Previously it was shown that the CD was 2.34%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The critical dilution value determines which WET test protocol applies; interpreting whether 2.34% is the operative CD for this permit term changes required test type and frequency.

candidates.exact_span: When the critical dilution is equal to or less than 10%, in lieu of the 7-day chronic test, a 48-hour acute test may be run using a 10:1 acute to chronic ratio; 23.4% rounded to the nearest whole number 23%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The CD threshold, optional-versus-mandatory acute testing language ('may be run'), and the 10:1 ratio with rounding to 23% govern which WET test method and dilution endpoints are required; different interpretations change monitoring obligation specifications.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall conduct a 48-hour acute test using Daphnia pulex once per quarter, and a 48-hour acute test using Pimephales promelas once per quarter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Quarterly acute tests for two species set explicit WET monitoring frequency and species requirements; interpreting quarter boundaries and species coverage changes expected monitoring counts for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: After the first four quarters without failures, the permittee may apply for a frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frequency reduction is conditional on four failure-free quarters and requires an application; interpreting whether reduction was granted or in effect during FY2025 changes applicable monitoring frequency (B) and how missing later-quarter tests are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any failure afterwards shall re-establish all tests for both species to once per quarter for the remainder of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A post-failure reset to quarterly testing for both species is a condition-triggered obligation change; interpreting what constitutes a failure and when it occurred alters required monitoring frequency (B) and whether absent results reflect a documented conditional state or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The test series will be 10%, 13%, 17%, 23% and 31%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The specified dilution series defines the required WET test concentrations; interpreting which dilutions must be run in each test affects whether conducted monitoring satisfied permit conditions.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall conduct separate whole effluent toxicity tests in accordance with Table 2:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reference to Table 2 for separate WET tests implies additional test requirements beyond the quarterly acute tests described above; interpreting what Table 2 requires (not present in this segment) affects the full set of applicable WET monitoring obligations.
